title: Algorithm 1: Empirical Quadrature Calibration (EQC)
text: Algorithm 1 (Empirical Quadrature Calibration). Input: Target reliability \rho^*, number items , latent distribution G, item parameter distribution H, quadrature size M, search bounds [c_L, c_U], tolerance \varepsilon. Step 1 (Quadrature Sampling). Draw \{\theta_m\}_{m=1}^M \sim G \{(\beta_i, \lambda_i^{(0)})\}_{=1}^\sim H. Fix samples subsequent evaluations. Step 2 (Empirical Reliability Function). Define \hat{\rho}_M : (0, \infty) \(0, 1) : \hat{\rho}_M(c) = \rho\bigl(c;\, \{\theta_m\}_{m=1}^M,\,   \boldsymbol{\beta},\, c \cdot \boldsymbol{\lambda}^{(0)}\bigr) using bracket-checked average-information reliability \tilde{\rho} (reliability_metric = "info" / "tilde"). Step 3 (Topology, Polishing, Selection). Scan x=\log(c) adaptively exact interval [c_L,c_U], refine detected extrema target features, polish every sign-changing bracket Brent’s method, select root root_policy. default selects lowest increasing crossing. Output: Calibrated scaling factor \hat{c}^*_M, achieved reliability \hat{\rho}_M(\hat{c}^*_M), calibrated item parameters.

title: Algorithm 1: Empirical Quadrature Calibration (EQC)
text: Theorem (Asymptotic Normality EQC). regularity conditions: \sqrt{M}\,(\hat{c}^*_M - c^*) \xrightarrow{d} N\!\left(0,\, \frac{\sigma^2_g}{g'(c^*)^2}\right) g(c) = \rho(c) - \rho^*, g'(c^*) = \rho'(c^*) slope reliability function solution, \sigma^2_g asymptotic variance \hat{g}_M(c^*). Proof sketch. Apply delta method (implicit function theorem version). CLT: \sqrt{M}\,\hat{g}_M(c^*) \xrightarrow{d} N(0, \sigma^2_g) Since \hat{c}^*_M solves \hat{g}_M(\hat{c}^*_M) = 0, Taylor expansion around c^* gives: 0 = \hat{g}_M(\hat{c}^*_M) \approx \hat{g}_M(c^*) + g'(c^*)\,(\hat{c}^*_M - c^*) Solving \hat{c}^*_M - c^* scaling \sqrt{M} yields result. key requirement g'(c^*) \neq 0, supplied strict local monotonicity selected branch.

text: Theorem (SAC Convergence; cf. Theorem .3, Lee 2026). Suppose: step sizes satisfy Eq. (4): \sum a_n = \infty, \sum a_n^2 < \infty. reliability function \rho(c) Lipschitz continuous [c_L, c_U]. g(c) = \rho(c) - \rho^* one isolated root c^* interior selected projected preflight branch. selected branch globally stable projection interval: (c-c^*)g(c)>0 every c\ne c^* interval, g'(c^*)>0 locally. noise \varepsilon_n satisfies \mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_n \mid c_n] = 0 \mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_n^2 \mid c_n] \leq \sigma^2_\varepsilon < \infty. projected SAC iterates converge almost surely: c_n \xrightarrow{\text{.s.}} c^* \quad \text{} n \\infty \qquad \text{(9)} local, branch-conditional result. claim globally unique root original user interval, apply reported branch_lost event. configured preflight scan supplies numerical evidence increasing branch; prove branch-wide drift condition assumed theorem. Proof sketch. proof follows classical Robbins-Monro theory, extended projected (constrained) setting Kushner Yin (2003, Chapter 5). key steps : Lyapunov function: Define V(c) = (c - c^*)^2. Compute conditional expectation V(c_{n+1}) given c_n:  \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}[V(c_{n+1}) \mid c_n] &= V(c_n) - 2a_n(c_n - c^*) g(c_n) + a_n^2 \mathbb{E}[(\hat{\rho}_n - \rho^*)^2 \mid c_n] \end{aligned} Drift condition: Since g(c)(c - c^*) > 0 c \neq c^* (reliability function increasing, g sign c - c^*), drift term -2a_n(c_n - c^*)g(c_n) < 0 provides contraction toward c^*. Noise control: accumulated noise \sum a_n^2 \sigma^2_\varepsilon < \infty (step size conditions), noise prevent convergence. Almost sure convergence: Robbins-Siegmund theorem (supermartingale convergence result), V(c_n) \V^* .s. random variable V^*. drift condition forces V^* = 0, giving c_n \c^* .s.

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: vignette provides comprehensive reference every exported function IRTsimrel v0.3.0. Functions organized five categories: Calibration Functions – core algorithms reliability-targeted simulation (eqc_calibrate, sac_calibrate, compare_eqc_sac). Simulation Functions – Generators latent abilities, item parameters, response data (sim_latentG, sim_item_params, simulate_response_data, compare_shapes). Reliability Functions – Low-level utilities computing exploring reliability (compute_rho_bar, compute_rho_tilde, compute_rho_both, compute_apc_init, check_feasibility, rho_curve, compute_reliability_tam). S3 Methods – Print, summary, plot, coef, predict, coercion methods object classes. Deprecated Functions – Legacy aliases retained backward compatibility (spc_calibrate, compare_eqc_spc). conceptual introductions, see vignette("introduction"). applied workflow guidance, see vignette("applied-guide"). mathematical theory, see vignette("theory-reliability"). Citation: Lee, J.-H. (2026). Reliability-Targeted Simulation Item Response Data: Solving Inverse Design Problem. arXiv:2512.16012v2. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2512.16012

title: Complete API Reference with Examples
text: Implements Algorithm 1 (EQC) Lee (2026). Given target marginal reliability, EQC draws large fixed quadrature sample abilities item parameters, maps reliability topology requested log-scale interval, applies explicit root-selection policy. Brent’s method (uniroot()) locally polishes ordinary sign-changing crossings; boundary, tangent, plateau, infeasible best-achievable outcomes follow separate contracts. recommended starting point simulation studies targets average-information metric.

title: Applied Guide: Reliability-Targeted IRT Simulation
text: investing computation time calibration, verify target reliability achievable. check_feasibility() evaluates reliability metrics across range scaling factors reports achievable interval. output reports resolved range average-information metric (\tilde{\rho}) MSEM-based metric (\bar{w}) one finite Monte Carlo design. target falls outside range, infeasible within configured bounds sampled design. Inspect topology best-achievable record deciding whether justify wider bounds, add items, change item model. finite heavy-tail MSEM range sensitivity evidence , population feasibility certificate. Quick check specific target:
code: feas <- check_feasibility(   n_items      = 25,   model        = "rasch",   latent_shape = "normal",   item_source  = "parametric",   target_rho   = 0.85,   c_bounds     = c(0.1, 10),   M            = 5000L,   seed         = 42 ) #>  #> ======================================================= #>   Feasibility Check: Achievable Reliability Range #> ======================================================= #>  #>   Number of items  : 25 #>   Model            : RASCH #>   Latent shape     : normal #>   Latent variance  : 1.0099 #>   c range          : [0.10, 10.00] #>   Monte Carlo M    : 5000 #>  #> Achievable Reliability Ranges: #>   rho_tilde (info) : [0.0591, 0.9872] #>   rho_bar   (msem) : [0.0002, 0.9146] #>  #> Target rho*        : 0.8500 #>   info status      : feasible #>   msem status      : feasible #>  #> Note: rho_tilde >= rho_bar on the same information grid (Jensen's inequality). #>   rho_tilde range screens EQC targets; root policy must still admit a root. #>   rho_bar range screens SAC targets; stable interior-branch preflight is also required. target <- 0.85 in_range <- identical(feas$target_status_info_canonical, "feasible") admissible <- feas$admissible_root_count_info > 0L cat(sprintf("Target rho = %.2f is %s for this design.\n",             target,             ifelse(in_range && admissible,                    "FEASIBLE WITH AN ADMISSIBLE ROOT",                    "NOT YET CALIBRATION-READY"))) #> Target rho = 0.85 is FEASIBLE WITH AN ADMISSIBLE ROOT for this design.

# ============================================================ # Reliability-Targeted IRT Simulation: Complete Workflow # ============================================================ library(IRTsimrel)  # --- Configuration ------------------------------------------ target_rho   <- 0.85       # desired marginal reliability n_items      <- 25         # test length model        <- "rasch"    # "rasch", "2pl", or "3pl" latent_shape <- "normal"   # latent distribution shape item_source  <- "parametric" item_params  <- if (model == "3pl") {   list(guessing_params = list(distribution = "fixed", value = 0.20)) } else {   list() } N_persons    <- 500        # sample size for response data M_quad       <- 5000L      # Monte Carlo samples for EQC seed_val     <- 42         # for reproducibility  # --- Step 1: Feasibility ------------------------------------ feas <- check_feasibility(   n_items = n_items, model = model,   latent_shape = latent_shape, item_source = item_source,   item_params = item_params,   target_rho = target_rho, M = M_quad, seed = seed_val, verbose = FALSE ) stopifnot(   identical(feas$target_status_info_canonical, "feasible"),   feas$admissible_root_count_info > 0L ) cat("Step 1: Feasible target with an admissible root confirmed.
")  # --- Step 2: Reliability curve (optional) -------------------- curve_df <- rho_curve(   n_items = n_items, model = model,   latent_shape = latent_shape, item_source = item_source,   item_params = item_params,   M = M_quad, seed = seed_val, plot = FALSE )  # --- Step 3: EQC calibration -------------------------------- eqc_res <- eqc_calibrate(   target_rho = target_rho, n_items = n_items,   model = model, latent_shape = latent_shape,   item_source = item_source,   item_params = item_params,   reliability_metric = "info",   M = M_quad, seed = seed_val ) cat(sprintf("Step 3: EQC calibrated c* = %.4f, achieved rho = %.4f
",             eqc_res$c_star, eqc_res$achieved_rho))  # --- Step 4: SAC validation (optional) ---------------------- sac_res <- sac_calibrate(   target_rho = target_rho, n_items = n_items,   model = model, latent_shape = latent_shape,   reliability_metric = "info",   c_init = eqc_res,   resample_items = FALSE,   n_iter = 200L, M_per_iter = 500L, M_pre = 5000L,   seed = seed_val ) cat(sprintf("Step 4: SAC calibrated c* = %.4f
", sac_res$c_star))  # --- Step 5: Generate response data ------------------------- sim_data <- simulate_response_data(   result = eqc_res, n_persons = N_persons,   latent_shape = latent_shape, seed = 123 ) cat(sprintf("Step 5: Generated %d x %d response matrix.
",             nrow(sim_data$response_matrix),             ncol(sim_data$response_matrix)))  # --- Step 6: Extract results -------------------------------- item_params <- coef(eqc_res) cat(sprintf("Step 6: Extracted %d item parameters.
", nrow(item_params)))

text: replication, : Generate response data calibrated model. Estimate item difficulties using simple proportion-based method (log-odds item proportion correct). Compute bias RMSE difficulty recovery. use log-odds difficulty estimator fast, base-R alternative full IRT estimation. avoids dependency external estimation packages. log-odds estimator : \hat{\beta}_i = -\log\left(\frac{p_i}{1 - p_i}\right) p_i proportion correct responses item . fast Rasch-oriented descriptive estimator, fitted 2PL estimator. case study therefore illustrates workflow; isolate pure model effect estimator misspecification 2PL cells.
code: # Storage cs1_results <- data.frame(   cell = integer(), rep = integer(),   model = character(), target_rho = numeric(),   bias_beta = numeric(), rmse_beta = numeric(),   max_abs_err = numeric(),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  for (i in seq_len(nrow(cs1_design))) {   d <- cs1_design[i, ]    for (r in seq_len(R)) {     # Generate data     sim <- simulate_response_data(       result    = cs1_calib[[i]],       n_persons = n_persons,       seed      = 1000 * i + r     )      # True item difficulties     beta_true <- sim$beta      # Estimate difficulties via item proportion correct     # Use log-odds transformation: beta_hat = -log(p / (1-p))     p_items <- colMeans(sim$response_matrix)     # Clip extreme proportions to avoid Inf     p_items <- pmin(pmax(p_items, 0.001), 0.999)     beta_hat <- -log(p_items / (1 - p_items))      # Center both for comparability (Rasch identification)     beta_hat <- beta_hat - mean(beta_hat)      # Compute metrics     bias       <- mean(beta_hat - beta_true)     rmse       <- sqrt(mean((beta_hat - beta_true)^2))     max_abs    <- max(abs(beta_hat - beta_true))      cs1_results <- rbind(cs1_results, data.frame(       cell = i, rep = r,       model = d$model, target_rho = d$target_rho,       bias_beta = bias, rmse_beta = rmse,       max_abs_err = max_abs,       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ))   } }

text: following template can adapted simulation study using IRTsimrel. Replace bracketed comments study’s parameters.
code: # ============================================================= # IRTsimrel Simulation Study Template # ============================================================= # # Research Question: #   [State your research question here] # # Author: JoonHo Lee (jlee296@ua.edu) # Date:   2026-07-01 # =============================================================  library(IRTsimrel)  # ---- 1. Design ---- design <- expand.grid(   target_rho   = c(0.60, 0.70, 0.80),      # [your reliability levels]   n_items      = c(20, 40),                  # [your test lengths]   model        = c("rasch", "2pl"),          # add "3pl" plus item_params when needed   latent_shape = c("normal", "skew_pos"),    # [your latent shapes]   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  N_PERSONS  <- 1000     # [your sample size] R          <- 500      # [your replications] M_QUAD     <- 10000L   # [your quadrature size] CALIB_SEED <- 42       # [your calibration seed]  # ---- 2. Feasibility screening ---- design$feasible <- NA for (i in seq_len(nrow(design))) {   feas <- check_feasibility(     n_items      = design$n_items[i],     model        = design$model[i],     latent_shape = design$latent_shape[i],     item_source  = "parametric",     target_rho   = design$target_rho[i],     M            = M_QUAD,     seed         = CALIB_SEED,     verbose      = FALSE   )   design$feasible[i] <-     identical(feas$target_status_info_canonical, "feasible") &&     feas$admissible_root_count_info > 0L } design <- design[design$feasible, ] cat(sprintf("Feasible cells: %d\n", nrow(design)))  # ---- 3. Calibration ---- calib_list <- vector("list", nrow(design)) for (i in seq_len(nrow(design))) {   d <- design[i, ]   calib_list[[i]] <- eqc_calibrate(     target_rho   = d$target_rho,     n_items      = d$n_items,     model        = d$model,     latent_shape = d$latent_shape,     item_source  = "parametric",     reliability_metric = "info",     M            = M_QUAD,     seed         = CALIB_SEED,     verbose      = FALSE   ) }  # ---- 4. Verification ---- design$achieved_rho <- vapply(calib_list,   function(r) r$achieved_rho, numeric(1)) design$abs_error <- abs(design$achieved_rho - design$target_rho) cat(sprintf("Max calibration error: %.2e\n", max(design$abs_error)))  # ---- 5. Simulation loop ---- output <- data.frame()  for (i in seq_len(nrow(design))) {   d <- design[i, ]    for (r in seq_len(R)) {     sim <- simulate_response_data(       result       = calib_list[[i]],       n_persons    = N_PERSONS,       latent_shape = d$latent_shape,       seed         = 1000 * i + r     )     sim_provenance <- sim$provenance[c("metric", "calibration_status",                                        "status_flags", "item_source",                                        "simulation_seed", "latent_shape")]      # ---- Your analysis here ----     beta_true <- sim$beta     p_items <- colMeans(sim$response_matrix)     p_items <- pmin(pmax(p_items, 0.001), 0.999)     beta_hat <- -log(p_items / (1 - p_items))     beta_hat <- beta_hat - mean(beta_hat)     rmse <- sqrt(mean((beta_hat - beta_true)^2))     bias <- mean(beta_hat - beta_true)      output <- rbind(output, data.frame(       cell = i, rep = r,       target_rho = d$target_rho, model = d$model,       n_items = d$n_items, latent_shape = d$latent_shape,       rmse = rmse, bias = bias,       metric = sim_provenance$metric,       calibration_status = sim_provenance$calibration_status,       simulation_seed = sim_provenance$simulation_seed     ))   } }  # ---- 6. Summarize ---- summary_table <- aggregate(   cbind(rmse, bias) ~ target_rho + model + n_items + latent_shape,   data = output, FUN = mean ) print(summary_table)

title: Generating Realistic Item Parameters
text: using source = "irw" source = "parametric" model = "2pl" model = "3pl", can choose discriminations generated. default method = "copula", three methods available.

title: Generating Realistic Item Parameters
text: rank-based Gaussian copula method leaves sampled difficulty values unchanged approximately targeting requested discrimination marginal dependence finite form. supplied rho latent Gaussian dependence parameter; realized Pearson Spearman correlations stochastic guaranteed equal . Algorithm: Transform \beta uniform scores: u = \{\text{rank}(\beta)-0.5\}/n. Transform normal: z_\beta = \Phi^{-1}(u). Generate correlated normal: z_\lambda = \rho \cdot z_\beta + \sqrt{1-\rho^2} \cdot z_{\text{indep}}. Transform uniform: v = \Phi(z_\lambda). Transform log-normal: \lambda = \exp(\mu + \sigma \cdot \Phi^{-1}(v)). copula recommended: Preserves exact difficulty distribution. Approximately targets log-normal discrimination marginal finite form. Uses rho latent-Gaussian dependence input; realized Pearson Spearman correlations stochastic inspected. Works well difficulty distribution shape.
code: items_copula <- sim_item_params(   n_items = 100,   model   = "2pl",   source  = "parametric",   method  = "copula",   discrimination_params = list(     mu_log    = 0,     sigma_log = 0.3,     rho       = -0.3   ),   seed = 42 )  # Check achieved correlation cat(sprintf("Target rho: -0.30\n")) #> Target rho: -0.30 cat(sprintf("Achieved Spearman: %.3f\n",             items_copula$achieved$overall$cor_spearman_pooled)) #> Achieved Spearman: -0.237

title: Generating Realistic Item Parameters
text: Uses conditional normal regression: \log(\lambda_i) \mid \beta_i \sim N\!\left(\mu_{\log} + \rho \cdot \sigma_{\log} \cdot z_{\beta_i}, \; \sigma_{\log}\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\right) Note: conditional method assumes linear relationships normal errors. empirical non-normal difficulties used, achieved correlations may differ targets.
code: items_cond <- sim_item_params(   n_items = 100,   model   = "2pl",   source  = "parametric",   method  = "conditional",   discrimination_params = list(rho = -0.3),   seed    = 42 )  cat(sprintf("Achieved Pearson:  %.3f\n",             items_cond$achieved$overall$cor_pearson_pooled)) #> Achieved Pearson:  -0.302 cat(sprintf("Achieved Spearman: %.3f\n",             items_cond$achieved$overall$cor_spearman_pooled)) #> Achieved Spearman: -0.310

title: Generating Realistic Item Parameters
text: scale parameter central reliability-targeted framework. multiplies discriminations constant factor: \lambda_i^* = c \cdot \lambda_{,0} \lambda_{,0} baseline discrimination c scale factor. 3PL item, full response probability P(Y_i=1\mid\theta)=g_i+(1-g_i) \operatorname{logit}^{-1}\{c\lambda_{,0}(\theta-\beta_i)\}. Thus, scale = c multiplies discrimination. scale lower asymptote: use guessing_params (custom_params$guessing) define g_i. Calibration functions estimate global c holding generated \beta_i g_i fixed.

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: sim_latentG() function generates latent abilities (person parameters \theta) IRT simulation studies. implements population model: \theta_p \sim G G flexible distribution family can take many different shapes maintaining rigorous standardization properties. Estimated reading time: 20–25 minutes. vignette covers: pre-standardization principle Available distribution shapes (12 supported shapes including custom) Customizing shape parameters Creating custom mixture distributions Adding covariate effects Visualization tools latent shape affects achievable reliability complete applied workflow uses sim_latentG() part reliability-targeted simulation, see vignette("applied-guide").

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: key design feature sim_latentG() pre-standardization: every built-distribution shape mathematically constructed mean 0 variance 1 scaling applied. ensures : Changing shape inadvertently change scale sigma parameter directly controls residual standard deviation; covariate variation can increase marginal SD theta Comparisons across shapes meaningful generated abilities follow: \theta_p = \mu + X_p^\top \beta + \sigma \cdot z_p z_p \sim G_0 \mathbb{E}[z] = 0 \text{Var}[z] = 1.

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: traditional simulation approaches, changing latent distribution often changes shape scale simultaneously. example, switching N(0, 1) \text{Gamma}(4, 1) changes just shape also variance. pre-standardization, can study effect distributional shape IRT estimation holding variance constant – cleaner experimental design.

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: output shows: Target mu/sigma: requested location scale Sample Moments: Empirical mean, SD, skewness, excess kurtosis
code: # Generate 1000 standard normal abilities sim_normal <- sim_latentG(n = 1000, shape = "normal", seed = 42)  # Examine the result print(sim_normal) #> Latent Ability Distribution (G-family) #> ======================================= #>   Shape     : normal #>   n         : 1000 #>   Target mu : 0.0000 #>   Target sigma: 1.0000 #>  #> Sample Moments: #>   Mean      : -0.0258 #>   SD        : 1.0025 #>   Skewness  : -0.0038 #>   Kurtosis  : 0.1286 (excess) # Verify standardization cat(sprintf("Sample mean: %.4f (target: 0)\n", mean(sim_normal$theta))) #> Sample mean: -0.0258 (target: 0) cat(sprintf("Sample SD:   %.4f (target: 1)\n", sd(sim_normal$theta))) #> Sample SD:   1.0025 (target: 1)

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: sim_latentG() provides 12 supported shapes, including 11 built-pre-standardized shapes plus custom mixture option.

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: baseline case: z \sim N(0, 1)
code: sim_normal <- sim_latentG(n = 2000, shape = "normal", seed = 1) plot(sim_normal, show_normal = TRUE)

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: symmetric two-component Gaussian mixture, useful representing populations two distinct subgroups (e.g., native vs. non-native speakers). Mathematical construction: z = s \cdot \delta + \epsilon, \quad s \sim \text{Rademacher}(\pm 1), \quad \epsilon \sim N(0, 1 - \delta^2) component variance 1 - \delta^2 ensures \text{Var}[z] = \delta^2 + (1 - \delta^2) = 1.  Customizing mode separation: delta parameter controls far apart modes (0 < \delta < 1):
code: sim_bimodal <- sim_latentG(n = 2000, shape = "bimodal", seed = 1) plot(sim_bimodal, show_normal = TRUE) # Wider separation sim_bimodal_wide <- sim_latentG(   n = 2000,   shape = "bimodal",   shape_params = list(delta = 0.95),   seed = 1 ) plot(sim_bimodal_wide, show_normal = TRUE)

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: symmetric three-component mixture central peak two side peaks. Mathematical construction: Components \{-m, 0, +m\} weights (w_L, w_0, w_R) w_L = w_R = (1 - w_0)/2. Component variance: \sigma_c^2 = 1 - (1 - w_0) m^2  Customizing:
code: sim_trimodal <- sim_latentG(n = 2000, shape = "trimodal", seed = 1) plot(sim_trimodal, show_normal = TRUE) # Stronger central peak sim_trimodal_central <- sim_latentG(   n = 2000,   shape = "trimodal",   shape_params = list(     w0 = 0.5,   # Weight of central component (default: 1/3)     m = 1.3     # Location of side components (default: 1.2)   ),   seed = 1 ) plot(sim_trimodal_central, show_normal = TRUE)

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: symmetric four-component mixture modes \{-m_2, -m_1, +m_1, +m_2\}.
code: sim_multi <- sim_latentG(n = 2000, shape = "multimodal", seed = 1) plot(sim_multi, show_normal = TRUE)

title: Working with Latent Distributions
text: Right-skewed (skew_pos): Based standardized Gamma distribution: z = \frac{\Gamma(k, 1) - k}{\sqrt{k}} \mathbb{E}[z] = 0 \text{Var}[z] = 1 k > 0.  Left-skewed (skew_neg): Simply negation right-skewed distribution.  Controlling skewness magnitude: k parameter (Gamma shape) controls skewness – smaller values mean skewed:

Even simplest Rasch case normal G, analytic inversion possible. Distribution dependence: mapping c \mapsto \rho(c) depends full distributions G (latent traits) H (item parameters), just moments. Metric ambiguity: two reliability definitions yield different c^* values target (Corollary 1). Practical constraints: scaling factor must lie within bounds produce realistic item parameters. APC initial value : c_{\text{APC}} = \sqrt{\frac{\rho^*}{\cdot \kappa \cdot (1 - \rho^*)}} \qquad \text{(25)} approximation typically within factor 2 true c^* serves starting point stochastic approximation algorithm (SAC).

what: Downstream DIF and score-recovery smoke evidence
title: Validation Evidence and Interpretation
text: primary practical pilot used one bounded mechanism: D = 1 3PL, fixed guessing 0.20, 20 items, 500 persons per group, 20 paired replications, three arms (c=1, target 0.60, target 0.80). Null four-item DIF conditions shared item, person, uniform random streams across arms. evidence contains 60 calibration rows, 400 fixed-form item rows, 120 replicate-arm- condition rows, 2,400 item-level Mantel–Haenszel rows. 17 blocking QA checks passed; maximum independent holdout error targeted arms 0.0171. Paired DIF-power differences -0.1625 target 0.60 minus c=1 (20-replicate t interval [-0.2497, -0.0753]) +0.2000 target 0.80 minus c=1 ([0.0887, 0.3113]). Within prespecified mechanism, discrimination/reliability scaling altered detection. establish higher target reliability always improves operating characteristics: null rejection rejection among non-DIF items also changed. secondary TAM arm contained three fits per arm (nine total), 180 item rows, 2,700 person rows, 549 information-curve rows. Mean EAP correlations c=1, target 0.60, target 0.80 0.834, 0.735, 0.883; mean EAP RMSEs 0.544, 0.666, 0.463. Eight nine fits reached 30-iteration cap, recovery exploratory. partial response reviewer’s practical-significance criticism, resolution. pilot 20 DIF replications, one test length, one guessing level, one DIF magnitude, internal-MH validation, purification. Moreover, fixed difficulty shift 0.50 changes response-logit magnitude global discrimination scale changes, contrast paired scale intervention rather pure causal effect reliability label. Publication-scale Type-/power claims require larger factorial study external DIF implementation.

title: IRTsimrel
text: IRTsimrel uses P(Y_{pi}=1\mid\theta_p) = g_i + (1-g_i)\operatorname{logit}^{-1}   \{c\lambda_{,0}(\theta_p-\beta_i)\}, \qquad D=1. names deliberately avoid common ambiguity: guessing item lower asymptote g_i; c global discrimination scale c_star calibrated value; calibration changes c\lambda_{,0}, change guessing item difficulty. sim_item_params() can generate fixed, beta-distributed, uniformly distributed guessing values. custom 3PL form supplies custom_params$guessing.

title: Analytic Pre-Calibration (APC) Initialization — compute_apc_init
text: Gaussian Rasch setting \(\theta \sim N(0,1)\) \(\beta \sim N(0, \sigma_\beta^2)\), expected item information involves logistic-normal convolution: $$\kappa(\sigma^2) = \int \frac{e^z}{(1+e^z)^2} \phi(z; 0, \sigma^2) dz$$ Approximating \(\kappa \approx 0.25 / \sqrt{1 + \sigma^2 \pi^2/3}\), closed-form pre-calibration : $$c_{init} = \sqrt{\frac{\rho^*}{\cdot \kappa \cdot (1 - \rho^*)}}$$

title: Compute Marginal Reliability from Simulated Test Information — compute_rho_bar
text: computation proceeds : Form scaled discriminations \(\lambda_i(c) = c \cdot \lambda_{,0}\). lower asymptote \(g_i\), compute \(p_{mi}=g_i+(1-g_i)\operatorname{logit}^{-1}       \{\lambda_i(c)(\theta_m-\beta_i)\}\) fixed D = 1 convention. Setting every \(g_i=0\) gives Rasch/2PL exactly. Compute 3PL item information \(\mathcal{J}_{mi}=\lambda_i(c)^2       (p_{mi}-g_i)^2(1-p_{mi})/\{(1-g_i)^2p_{mi}\}\). \(g_i=0\), reduces \(\lambda_i(c)^2p_{mi}(1-p_{mi})\). Test information \(\theta_m\): \(\mathcal{J}_m = \sum_i \mathcal{J}_{mi}\). Reliability: compute_rho_bar(): harmonic-mean-based MSEM \(\text{MSEM} = E[1/\mathcal{J}_m]\), \(\bar{w}(c) = \sigma_\theta^2 / (\sigma_\theta^2 + \text{MSEM})\). compute_rho_tilde(): arithmetic-mean-based information \(\bar{\mathcal{J}} = E[\mathcal{J}_m]\), \(\tilde{\rho}(c) = \sigma_\theta^2 \bar{\mathcal{J}} /           (\sigma_\theta^2 \bar{\mathcal{J}} + 1)\). Information expectations evaluated log domain. artificial information floor applied. Consequently, zero information positively weighted node correctly implies infinite MSEM zero MSEM-based reliability.

title: Compute Marginal Reliability from Simulated Test Information — compute_rho_bar
code: # Simple toy example set.seed(1) theta <- rnorm(1000) beta  <- rnorm(20) lambda0 <- rep(1, 20)  compute_rho_bar(1, theta, beta, lambda0) #> [1] 0.7795393 compute_rho_tilde(1, theta, beta, lambda0) #> [1] 0.7870079  # With pre-calculated theta variance (recommended for SAC) theta_var_fixed <- var(rnorm(10000))  # Pre-calculate from large sample compute_rho_bar(1, theta, beta, lambda0, theta_var = theta_var_fixed) #> [1] 0.7684109  # 3PL lower asymptotes use the same public kernel. g <- rep(0.20, length(beta)) compute_rho_tilde(1, theta, beta, lambda0, guessing = g) #> [1] 0.7055277

title: Empirical Quadrature Calibration (Algorithm 1: EQC) — eqc_calibrate
text: eqc_calibrate() implements Algorithm 1 (Empirical Quadrature Calibration, EQC) reliability-targeted IRT simulation. Given target marginal reliability \(\rho^*\), latent distribution generator sim_latentG() (\(G\)) item parameter generator sim_item_params() (\(H\)), function searches global discrimination scale \(c^* > 0\) selected empirical quadrature approximation \(\hat\rho_M(c)\) Rasch, 2PL, 3PL model matches \(\rho^*\). Population accuracy Monte Carlo approximation assessed independent draws. key idea : Draw large fixed "quadrature" sample \(\{\theta_m\}_{m=1}^M \sim G\) item parameters \(\{(\beta_i, \lambda_{,0})\}_{=1}^\sim H\) . scale \(c\), form \(\lambda_i(c) = c \cdot \lambda_{,0}\) compute empirical approximation population reliability \(\hat\rho_M(c)\) test information function. Scan explicit scale interval logarithmic grid, enumerate detected roots \(\hat\rho_M(c^*) = \rho^*\), apply requested branch-selection policy.

title: Empirical Quadrature Calibration (Algorithm 1: EQC) — eqc_calibrate
text: function calibrates average-information reliability definition: Average-information ("info"/"tilde", default): Uses arithmetic mean, \(\tilde{\rho}(c) = \sigma^2_\theta \bar{\mathcal{J}}(c) / (\sigma^2_\theta \bar{\mathcal{J}}(c) + 1)\). Jensen's inequality, \(\tilde{\rho} \geq \bar{w}\), metric typically yields higher reliability values. recommended default EQC objective function \(\tilde{\rho}(c) - \rho^*\) stable practical search intervals. implementation nevertheless scans complete user-supplied interval log(c), polishes detected local extrema successfully bracketed sign-changing crossings, records near-target fallback separately, applies explicit root policy. assume empirical curve globally monotone unimodal. MSEM-based ("msem"/"bar") reliability uses harmonic mean test information, \(\bar{w}(c) = \sigma^2_\theta / (\sigma^2_\theta + E[1/\mathcal{J}(\theta;c)])\). metric rejected eqc_calibrate() objective \(\bar{w}(c) - \rho^*\) may non-monotone (see reliability-targeted simulation manuscript, Section 4.3). Although shared scanner can diagnose topology, MSEM remains outside EQC's calibration contract. Use sac_calibrate need target \(\bar{w}\) directly.

title: Simulate Latent Ability Distribution for IRT Studies (G-family) — sim_latentG
text: sim_latentG() generates latent abilities (person parameters \(\theta\)) Item Response Theory (IRT) simulation studies. implements population model \(\theta_p \sim G\) \(G\) flexible distribution family. function designed two key principles: Pre-standardization: distribution shape mathematically constructed mean 0 variance 1, ensuring changing shape inadvertently change scale. Separation Structure Scale: sigma parameter directly controls standard deviation latent trait, independent distributional shape. generated abilities follow: $$\theta_p = \mu + X_p^\top \beta + \sigma \cdot z_p$$ \(z_p \sim G_0\) \(E[z]=0\) \(Var[z]=1\).

title: IRTsimrel 0.3.0
text: Added end--end support unidimensional three-parameter logistic model logistic scaling constant D = 1. shared model engine, reliability reducers, item generation, EQC, SAC, response simulation, S3 result methods now carry item lower asymptotes. Added fixed, beta, uniform guessing generators guessing_params; custom forms use custom_params$guessing. Values must satisfy 0 <= guessing < 1. Clarified parameter names: item guessing stored guessing (mathematical g_i), c/c_star global discrimination scale. Calibration applies lambda_i(c) = c * lambda_i0 never rescales guessing. guessing = 0 3PL path computationally identical 2PL path. Probability Fisher-information calculations use stable log-domain kernels extreme linear predictors.

title: IRTsimrel 0.3.0
text: EQC now scans complete user-supplied interval log(c), records resolved roots local extrema, applies explicit root policy. EQC remains fixed-form, average-information (info/tilde) calibrator. SAC now runs topology preflight Robbins–Monro updates, constrains trajectory selected branch, performs independent final evaluation. New controls appended historical argument prefix: root_policy, preflight_controls, evaluation_controls. SAC explicitly distinguishes resample_items = FALSE (fixed-form estimand) resample_items = TRUE (item-superpopulation estimand). Results store calibration/evaluation design metadata, achieved distributions standard errors, branch diagnostics, RNG provenance. EQC result warm starts accepted matching metric/model/item count fixed-form contract. -seed SAC replay caller RNG restoration enforced independent random-number streams. check_feasibility() rho_curve() use shared topology scanner rather assuming global monotonicity. Multiple roots remain possible adversarial poorly covered designs.

title: IRTsimrel 0.3.0
text: Reliability utilities now accept 3PL guessing vectors optional quadrature weights, return numerical/estimand diagnostics request. default scalar/list shapes remain backward compatible. New result schema fields include guessing_vec, schema_version, item_scope, estimand_signature, design_signature. Legacy Rasch/2PL results without guessing interpreted lazily zero-guessing designs mutated. Incomplete legacy spc_result objects now fail actionable instruction rerun sac_calibrate(). spc_calibrate() compare_eqc_spc() remain deprecated forwarding aliases. historical 18-argument prefix sac_calibrate() unchanged; new controls appended preserve positional calls. Reliability reduction automatically chunks transient item-information matrices preserving exact scalar results. Matrix-returning internal kernels retain previous full-output contract.

title: IRTsimrel 0.3.0

TAM::tam.wle() support fitted tam.mml.3pl object, IRTsimrel claim 3PL WLE support. public compute_reliability_tam() helper continues provide WLE EAP output documented Rasch/2PL paths.
